articles.title: Why Paying "Market Price" for Rare Pokémon Card Sets Somehow Became The New Normal
articles.summary: Pokémon TCG market prices often exceed MSRP, but they can help collectors avoid scalpers' worst prices, so here's why fans still rely on them.
body: Even for the biggest and most popular games, getting products at MSRP (Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price) should indeed be the norm; nevertheless, for those like the Pokémon TCG, ‘market price’ has become the go-to metric for many collectors for one big reason.
Depending on your perspective as a Pokemon fan, referring to the concept as a gateway to ‘inflated’ or ‘rip-off’ pricing is totally valid.

That said, when actually getting down to the logistics of what it means to get a box of new Pokémon cards at MSRP today, the “market price”, well, market — has been the response to a growing problem with the collectables market as a whole, and is still a legitimate way to enjoy the Pokémon TCG (very much within reason).
To first put it plainly before going into the nitty-gritty, the rise of paying “market price” for Pokemon cards over MSRP ultimately comes down to one classic concept: supply vs. demand.

articles.title: Why Games Workshop's Falling Share Price Is All of a Sudden in the News
articles.summary: Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes. Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years.
body: Broadly speaking, there seems to be investor nervousness at Games Workshop’s ability to keep growing in the face of rising manufacturing and logistics costs. Some on the internet will say the recently released 11th edition of flagship tabletop wargame Warhammer 40,000 hasn’t done as well as Games Workshop had hoped, but there is no official data to back this claim up. Indeed, in an update issued mid-September, Games Workshop said that trading to August 30 was “in line with the Board’s expectations for the current financial year.”

However, there is certainly a feeling that Games Workshop may have hit a wall in terms of the popularity of its tabletop games, particularly Warhammer 40,000, which has seen multiple new, pricey miniatures released recently amid claims of over-saturation.

Things ramped up last week with two reports from the financial press about the state of Games Workshop. The first, from the Financial Times, titled ‘Is Warhammer still winning?’ The FT pointed out that while GW’s financials are, broadly speaking, very positive, retail growth per store turned negative for the first time since the pandemic in the second half of its 2026 financial year.

Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years.

articles.title: 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' Author Officially Settles a Raging Debate About the Audiobooks
articles.summary: The series has become enormously popular, in large part because of its best-selling audiobooks performed by Jeff Hays. But fans often choose not to listen to Dinniman's lengthy books at the speed at which Hays performed them.
body: At what speed do you listen to your Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks? This is a major topic of discussion in the fandom for Matt Dinniman’s LitRPG series. The books are about a post-apocalyptic future where an alien corporation has taken over Earth, using up all its resources and killing most the humans. The survivors are forced to participate in a televised reality competition called Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. Among those competitors is a Coast Guard veteran named Carl, who is accompanied by a talking cat named Princess Donut.

At New York Comic Con, Polygon got a chance to sit down with author Dinniman. We asked about the progress of the upcoming Dungeon Crawler Carl live-action series and the future of LitRPG in general, but the most important query we had for him was all about the proper listening speed for DCC audiobooks.
Polygon: Fans have a lot of favorite characters. Would you ever be open to writing a spinoff starring another character?

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Dev Confirms DDoS Attack
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said. Players suffered intermittent disconnects and login issues while trying to play the Xbox Series X and S and PC action game, which The Coalition eventually got on top of.
body: “Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We’ll provide updates if there are any significant changes,” The Coalition said. “Thank you for your patience and understanding.”

There is a great deal of speculation online about the motivation behind hitting Gears with a DDoS attack, with some pointing to a continued online vendetta against the game for apparently being “woke.” E-Day has a “mostly positive” user review rating on Steam. Whatever the reason (there may be no overarching reason behind the DDoS attack at all), E-Day is now up and running.

Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales.

Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.

articles.title: Latest Leaked GTA 6 Video Shows Lucia Fully Naked, Sparks Fan Skepticism
articles.summary: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly released yet another unauthorized gameplay video, this time allegedly showing Lucia fully naked in a bid to push their crypto scheme. However, some now suspect Cyberleek is using a developer build or cheats to make Jason and Lucia naked, and that the leaked gameplay…
body: Cyberleek had threatened to release gameplay showing Lucia fully naked if the market cap of their memecoin hit $4 million. That was achieved over the weekend. However, while the new video reportedly does show Lucia fully naked, there are a number of signs that some believe suggest Cyberleek has tinkered with the build they allegedly have access to.

One suspected telltale sign from the previous leak was that a tank was spawned into the game world, suggesting access to a dev menu of some kind. Now, with two leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked but NPCs in the game world failing to react to that in any way, some believe this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.

One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

articles.title: For the second time this year, Steam has set a major new concurrent user record
articles.summary: There's clearly no stopping Steam's continued growth. Valve's PC digital store and social platform set a new user concurrent record on Sunday, with a staggering 43,505,724 million users (via SteamDB ).
body: Yes, that's over 43 million players online at the same time across the world, both in-game and out. Incidentally, the number of players in-game also went up to more than 14 million, itself a new record.

That is the highest ever number of simultaneous users in Steam's 23-year history. It's also the second time Valve's platform has broken its own record this year, having attracted over 42 million concurrent players in January.

Steam's Autumn Sale recently ended, so it's curious the new record was set shortly afterwards and not during the sale. That said, the last few weeks have seen a number of popular game launches, most notably the worldwide release of free-to-play MMO Aion 2, which peaked at 397,905 concurrent players at launch.

Steam's list of the top ten most played games remains mostly the same outside of that, except for the big jump in Deadlock numbers (262,145 peak concurrent) off the back of a major update. Deadlock is Valve's third-person MOBA-shooter hybrid, which the developer has yet to officially announce.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's lead actor reminds us why AI will always struggle to replicate a human performance
articles.summary: Will de Renzy-Martin, the actor who plays lead character Coen in the English language version of The Blood of Dawnwalker, has reminded us of the value humans bring to a performance, versus AIs generating voice lines.
body: Speaking in a TikTok teaser for an upcoming episode of the My Perfect Console Podcast, de Renzy-Martin highlighted how the spoken lines themselves are only half - if that - of what an actor brings. "I think the least interesting thing about what I do is the way my voice sounds," de Renzy-Martin said. "That is really all that generative AI is able to replicate.

"It's not replicating my personality and the things that I do when I'm in the room, and the choices that I make, which is all the reasons that a director or a producer would want to work with me. And there might be directors and producers who don't want to do those things [and to use AI], but then they've got to get really good at getting performances out of something - they need to have their own ideas."

The discussion reminded de Renzy-Martin of something he apparently said four or five years ago: "Actors are pretty cheap in the grand scheme of things. And if you end up with an AI that can produce the right noises, you're going to need somebody who can interact with it and get the performance that you want attached to those noises - and they're going to be much more expensive than an actor is."

articles.title: Josh Brolin Teases a Thanos vs. Doctor Doom Showdown in 'Avengers: Secret Wars'
articles.summary: At New York Comic Con 2026 this past weekend, Josh Brolin was on the ground to promote his new movie Whalefall. Directed by Brian Duffield and based on a novel by Daniel Kraus, Whalefall is the story of a scuba diver ( Resident Evil 's Austin Abrams) who gets swallowed whole by a sperm whale.
body: Polygon spoke with Brolin about Whalefall, which releases on Oct. 16, but we couldn't resist asking a Marvel question as well, since Brolin played Thanos in Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. With the upcoming release of Avengers: Doomsday, it seems that Robert Downey Jr.'s take on Doctor Doom may dethrone Brolin's Thanos as the Marvel Cinematic Universe's biggest-ever villain, so we asked Brolin, "Could Thanos take down Doctor Doom?" He seemed intruigied by the idea, suggesting a showdown could happen in a future MCU project — assuming Marvel Studios allowed it.
"I don't know," Brolin replied. "Any confrontation with Downey, I like the idea of. I love that he’s doing that, by the way. I can’t wait to see it."

Beyond that, Brolin didn't give a definitive answer to the showdown. But if the comics are any indication, Doctor Doom would at least be a formidable opponent for Thanos. In 2015's Secret Wars, Doctor Doom gained the powers of the Beyonders, and when he confronted Thanos, Doom ripped the Mad Titan's spine — skull included — from his body. Perhaps we'll see the same in 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars?

articles.title: Stardew Valley creator's new game, Haunted Chocolatier, is "more of an action RPG" than farming sim
articles.summary: Stardew Valley creator Eric Barone, has given a new interview - and finally revealed a little more information about his upcoming title, Haunted Chocolatier. In a wide-ranging interview with GQ, which tackles topics ranging from creative burnout to the importance of 'cosy gaming', Barone also slips…
body: And it's all rather surprising. Per the interview, this game is a much more action-oriented affair than the cosy homesteading of Stardew Valley: "It is still what I call a town game," he told GQ, "but it's more of an action RPG - the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights."

For anyone that's played Stardew Valley, this won't be a massive shock; there is a combat element to the game, though mostly it's sequestered to one portion of the map - the mines that hold some of the game's rarest materials. If you had fun venturing in there at night to fight slimes and horde minerals, you're going to like Haunted Chocolatier, it seems. "[The new game] is for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly," said Barone.

Elsewhere, Barone noted that Haunted Chocolatier is a more "metaphysical" experience than Stardew Valley - which makes sense, I suppose, given its connection to the world of ghosts and spirits - and that "no one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it". Hence, there's still no word on a solid release date.

articles.title: 'Carrie' Showrunner Confirms the Biggest Changes to the Book Were Stephen King's Idea
articles.summary: When Mike Flanagan set out to adapt Stephen King 's classic 1970 novella into an eight-episode series set in 2026, the first thing he did was go to King himself.
body: "There's no world where I'm doing anything like that without talking to Steve about it first," Flanagan tells Polygon. "He got to see all of that before I agreed to do the show, and was very intimately involved in deciding how we wanted to expand that universe."

The result is Carrie, which is streaming now on Prime Video and generating quite a lot of debate among Stephen King fans over the many ways it alters the source material. So when Polygon had the chance to interview Flanagan about his new show, one of the first things we asked was what King himself thought about all those changes. Turns out, not only was the legendary author directly involved, but some of the biggest changes were actually his idea.

"Some people seem animated by trying to protect Stephen King in this, and what I want to say to them is, 'Guys, this is Steve's idea,'" Flanagan says. "Steve believed very much that the story had already been told as he had written it. What excited him and animated him about this was the chance to expand that universe and to open it up into a much broader world."

articles.title: DMZ for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 being released early, but Infinity Ward shoots down PvE hopes
articles.summary: In yet another surprising move for Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4 studio Infinity Ward has announced that the game's extraction shooter mode, DMZ, will be released prior to the game's official launch. DMZ will be available starting 20th October for players who pre-order a copy digitally.
body: Modern Warfare 4 now effectively has three release dates. The campaign unlocks 16th October, DMZ four days later on the 20th, and the full launch - which is when multiplayer will be playable - arrives 23rd October.

Though Infinity Ward has offered campaign early access with other Modern Warfare titles in the past, doing the same for DMZ - a multiplayer mode - is certainly new. It's a potentially shrewd move, allowing DMZ to capture streamers and generate excitement about the game ahead of its release over an entire week, with a big blip every few days. It also allows players curious about DMZ to play it without feeling they ought to be making progress in multiplayer instead.

Seeing as DMZ has its own separate progression, however, players who jump in early could potentially have an advantage come launch if they manage to accrue many items, not to mention the map knowledge they would get from simply spending more time playing.
points: In yet another surprising move for Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4 studio Infinity Ward has announced that the game's extraction shooter mode, DMZ, will be released prior to the game's official launch.
DMZ will be available starting 20th October for players who pre-order a copy digitally.

articles.title: 33 Years Later, Tom Cruise's Near-Perfect Legal Thriller Is Officially on Streaming
articles.summary: Tom Cruise has built a career playing men who find themselves in increasingly dangerous situations, whether by choice or by sheer bad luck. From dangling off a skyscraper in Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol to running for his life in War of the Worlds to navigating the increasingly bizarre…
body: However, some of his best work came long before he was hanging off airplanes and outrunning explosions, back when he was building a reputation as one of Hollywood’s most compelling leading men. Among the many excellent films in Cruise’s early career, The Firm deserves a place near the top of the list. Directed by Sydney Pollack and based on John Grisham’s bestselling 1991 novel, the legal thriller finds Cruise playing a young lawyer whose dream job quickly turns into a waking nightmare. It’s a different kind of Cruise movie by today's standards, trading globe-trotting spectacle for mounting paranoia, but The Firm is worth checking out now that it's streaming on Paramount Plus.

The story follows Mitch McDeere (Cruise), a brilliant Harvard Law School graduate who accepts an offer from a prestigious Memphis law firm with a suspiciously generous compensation package. The firm provides him with a house, a luxury car, and a level of financial security that seems almost too good to pass up. His wife, Abby (Jeanne Tripplehorn), is understandably thrilled with their new life, and Mitch has every reason to believe he’s finally made it.

articles.title: Here come the weird and wonderful mods for the Steam Frame, as Valve drops the full CAD files for free
articles.summary: Valve has released the CAD files for the Steam Frame, allowing modders the perfect opportunity to get to work on their own creations for the VR headset. The light blocker—the bit that sits between the bridge of your nose and the headset—is primed for user replacement, as are the head strap, battery…
body: Valve has confirmed it is working on an upgraded head strap with interchangeable batteries and off-ear speakers for the Steam Frame. That's " coming soon ". With this CAD release, perhaps we'll see more options for third parties in future, too.

The docs also detail how to interface with the expansion port, or auxiliary port as Valve calls it. This sits just to the front of the user's nose and is a way for a user to add in powered accessories, ie the Arcturus Vision RGB camera—I've been playing around with that for a couple of weeks and it's a pretty wicked upgrade. With one Gen4 PCIe lane alongside power and camera functionality, all laid out in the docs, there's a bunch more that could be done with the port. I'm just hoping someone runs with it.

With this release, Valve has a full sweep of CAD files available for all of its most recent products. There's the Steam Deck, Steam Machine, Steam Controller, and now Steam Frame. That's how it should be done, people.

articles.title: 'The algorithm continues to properly prioritise Mister Biddy Blas'—Star Wars: Galactic Racer has created the perfect creature
articles.summary: Star Wars: Galactic Racer is out, and it's pretty solid, netting a firm 76 score in our Galactic Racer review. It's also, as should always be the case with Star Wars videogames, full of funny little guys. None so funny as Biddy Blas. Why is Biddy Blas so popular?
body: I'm not even really seeking out much Galactic Racer content, and this guy's been cropping up on my recommended feeds, as observed by Lucasfilm Games executive producer Craig Derrick on X: "The algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it."

Blas is, in essence, a perfect "Glup Shitto". A fake character used as a sort of symbolic memetic stand-in for obscure Star Wars background characters that somehow become people's favourites. Blas isn't the first crocin to make an appearance in Star Wars, however—that was in Solo: A Star Wars Story.

Which is a relatively recent addition for Glup status, and as such I can't tell you much about the Crocin, other than the fact they apparently need to wear those goggles to protect their sensitive eyes from harsh sunlight. Owing to the fact that, on their home planet, they live in big caverns.

For Biddy Blas, however, I can only imagine he needs them to avoid scalding his sclera from the shine of his glorious racing prowess-slash-approaching intergalactic fandom. Which he insists that he already has—hard-earned via a supposed stint as a Huttball player and jatz trumpeter (not to be confused with another music genre, jizz).

articles.title: Explore the town of Detour in this new Fallout 4 mod chock full of voiced NPCs and quests
articles.summary: A group of veteran Fallout 4 modders have just added a whole new town to its wasteland, offering another place to pop into for some trading and questing as you roam post-apocalyptic Boston.
body: Drawing a bit of inspiration from Fallout 3 's Arefu and Highway Town from Fallout 76 's Burning Springs update, Detour 's a settlement up on one of the ruined freeways which loom above parts of the wasteland. It's not too far from vanilla starting location Sanctuary, near the map marker for Bedford Station, so it's an ideal place to visit early on in a playthrough.

The town's home to voiced citizens running shops, offering to rent you a room, or keeping the peace. There's a ghoul sheriff and a mayor who seem prime candidates to offer up a quest or two, with the former's digs indicating he's got work for bounty hunters, and a thief named Randy looking like he might have something for you to do if you spring him from the can. Plus, there's a house you can buy if you fancy moving in permanently.

videos.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered: PC Performance Review + Optimised Settings
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring our PC performance reviews. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: Note on texture quality/VRAM: The on-screen VRAM figures are from RTX 5090 testing at 4K DLAA with RT disabled. The recommendation of High textures for 8GB GPUs is based on separate RTX 4060 testing, also with RT disabled, where VRAM usage remained below 7GB.

Having already delivered the Complete Edition, CD Projekt RED still has plans for The Witcher 3, hence the arrival of the controversial Remastered release - and while it has some key improvements, there are still some issues. In our PC performance review, we present the top-line changes to the game then compare the hotfix 5.00C version to the latest patch 5.01 before we dive head-first into those all-important optimised settings.
